Team — forwarding Elena's note. They need a proposal by Oct 5 for a leadership review on Oct 6. High-level ask is: multi-year (24–36m), staged ramp, co-term across two entities, EU invoicing, SOC2 evidence, auto-renew with opt-out, and a safety-net credit to mitigate year-1 overcommit.

I'm proposing we give them two options:

Option A — 24 months (co-term)
- Year 1: 50% committed of target consumption; Year 2: 125% of Year 1 committed (true-up at year end)
- 10% volume discount vs list across both entities if they commit to co-term
- Annual EU invoicing (local VAT handling), standard SOC2 package attached
- Auto-renew with 45-day opt-out window
- Safety-net: first-year 10% credit applied at renewal to offset shortfall (applies only if actual usage < committed)

Option B — 36 months (staggered onramp)
- Year 1: 40% commit; Year 2: 80% commit; Year 3: 140% of Year 1 commit (annual true-ups)
- 14% volume discount vs list for 36m co-term with billing annualized
- Quarterly usage reporting and per-route SLOs on the console
- Auto-renew opt-in (30-day opt-out) with a built-in "safety buffer" credit equal to 8% of year-1 committed value

Operational notes/asks for you:
- Kimberly: can you confirm whether we can provide the 14% across a 36m vs 10% on 24m? Need final discount authority.
- Karthik: is annual EU invoicing workable on our side (billing code, tax handling) and any constraints on staggering invoices across entities?
- Camila: CSM ops — will the onboarding checklist (attached) and a 60-day rollout plan be sufficient to avoid service interruptions when we ramp?

I've attached two stubs: NovaPulse_MultiYear_Options.xlsx (pricing matrix) and Ops_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (ops steps and required artifacts).

Goal: get internal alignment by Mon 9/28 so we can finalize a clean proposal to Elena by 10/5. Thoughts?

Marcus
